articles.title: Help EFF Solve an Issue That's Bigger than Creepy Ads
articles.summary: Microsoft just dropped 167 patches including a SharePoint zero-day and the deliciously named 'BlueHammer' Windows Defender vuln. When your Patch Tuesday count hits triple digits, you know someone's been busy breaking things.

articles.title: Grafana GitHub Token Breach Led to Codebase Download and Extortion Attempt
articles.summary: CVE-2026-42945 turns NGINX into a heap buffer overflow playground with active exploitation in the wild. Because apparently even the internet's favorite reverse proxy can't escape the tender embrace of RCE vulnerabilities.

articles.title: Anti-DDoS Firm Heaped Attacks on Brazilian ISPs
articles.summary: Canvas got pwned so hard it disrupted schools nationwide, with hackers defacing the login page like it's 2011 all over again. Nothing says 'digital education' quite like ransomware threatening to leak your homework assignments.

articles.title: MPs want social media treated more like unsafe toys than harmless apps
articles.summary: OpenAI employees got their machines compromised via poisoned npm packages in a classic supply chain attack. Even the AI overlords fall for the oldest trick in the book - malicious dependencies.

articles.title: Victory! End-to-End Encrypted RCS Comes to Apple and Android Chats
articles.summary: Instagram just killed its end-to-end encryption feature, breaking years of privacy promises faster than you can say 'Zuckerberg lied again.' Another beautiful encryption dream dies in the Facebook graveyard.

articles.title: EFF Launches New Offline Campaign for Saudi Wikipedian Osama Khalid
articles.summary: Finally! iPhone and Android users get encrypted RCS messaging, ending the green bubble surveillance nightmare. Only took them a decade to figure out that maybe our texts shouldn't be readable by every three-letter agency.

articles.title: The Boring Stuff is Dangerous Now
articles.summary: Saudi Wikipedian Osama Khalid, contributing since age 12, now needs our help fighting digital oppression. Because apparently editing Wikipedia and blogging about open source makes you dangerous to authoritarian regimes.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds a flaw in Microsoft Exchange Server to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: Pwn2Own Berlin 2026 ends with DEVCORE dominating the competition, discovering 47 zero-days and earning over $1.2M. When ethical hacking pays better than most day jobs, you know the industry is properly broken.

articles.title: OpenAI caught in TanStack npm supply chain chaos after employee devices compromised
articles.summary: Linus Torvalds declares the Linux security mailing list 'almost entirely unmanageable' thanks to AI bug hunters spamming duplicate findings. Even the kernel god can't escape the robot apocalypse cluttering his inbox.

articles.title: aegis-atv 0.5.1
articles.summary: AI-assisted researchers just broke Apple's M5 Memory Integrity Enforcement for root access on macOS using Anthropic's Claude. The machines are now teaching themselves to pwn other machines - we've officially reached peak irony.
